name: Nanocyte — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Nanocyte from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Nanocyte (Armorist Archetype)" but are not part of the Nanocyte entry, which is unchanged.

This replaces magic talents. This archetype may be combined with other archetypes that replace magic talents; the nanocyte cannot gain a combat or skill talent in place of a magic talent the other archetype loses.

Loadout Limitation

At 1st level, the nanocyte chooses one of the following limitations:

Fragile Construction: The nanocyte does not gain any bound equipment.
Limited Nanites: The nanocyte may not form a nanite array while she has summoned or bound equipment active, and may not summon equipment while a nanite array is formed. While her nanite array is not formed, the nanocyte may only summon 1 piece of equipment at a time, plus an additional piece of equipment at 10th and 20th levels.
Nanite Dedication: The nanocyte does not gain casting or a spell pool from nanocyte levels, and may not select magic talents from nanocyte levels. The nanocyte’s levels do not count as spherecasting levels. The nanocyte gains a surge pool, containing a number of surge points equal to her practitioner modifier + 1/4 her nanocyte level. This pool replenishes after 30 minutes of rest, or 15 minutes if you have access to reasonably comfortable accommodations (such as a bed, cushions, or other fineries of comfort). Whenever the nanocyte would spend a spell point to use or activate a nanocyte class feature, the nanocyte may instead expend a number of surge points equal to the number of spell points required by that ability.
Nanite Array (Ex)

At 1st level, the nanocyte’s body becomes host to an array of nanomachines which can take the form of either a cloud or a sheath. The nanocyte may cause her nanites to assume either array as a move action, or as a swift or immediate action by spending a spell point.

The nanites can only assume one array at a time, and the nanocyte may dismiss an array as a move action. The nanites maintain their array until the nanocyte directs them into a different array, she falls unconscious, or she ends her turn more than 10 feet from the array. If an array ends without being turned into a different array, the nanites disperse and return to the nanocyte’s body at the beginning of her next turn and await further instructions. If the nanocyte is not within close range of the array or the array is physically blocked from reaching her, the nanites instead break down, and the nanocyte cannot use her nanite array again until she spends 1 spell point and takes a full action to create a replacement array.

Array Improvements (Ex)

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the nanocyte selects an array improvement for both her cloud array and her sheath array. She may change which improvements she has selected for each array each time she gains a level.

Cloud Array Improvements
Anchoring Cloud: The nanocyte’s nanite cloud is considered difficult terrain for any creatures except the nanocyte.
Drifting Host: The nanocyte’s nanite cloud may be anywhere within close range of her without dispersing. This improvement may be selected up to three times, increasing the range from close to medium and from medium to long.
Expanded Cloud: The nanocyte’s cloud array may fill 4 additional 5-foot squares. This improvement may be selected multiple times.

Seeking Strikes: When making attacks against targets in her nanite cloud, the nanocyte ignores any miss chance from concealment. This improvement may be taken a second time, in which case the nanocyte ignores any bonuses from cover (but not total cover) for creatures in her nanite cloud.
Sensory Nanites: The nanocyte gains blindsense with a range of 5 feet. This blindsense also extends to any area in or adjacent to her cloud array. The nanocyte may take this improvement a second time. If she does, the blindsense improves to blindsight.
Split Cloud: You may have two instances of your nanite cloud active at a time, and may move or reform all of them as part of the same action. The total area of your nanite cloud is divided between these two clouds. You may select this improvement multiple times, each time gaining the ability to create an additional cloud.
Telepathic Cloud: You can communicate telepathically with any creatures within the area of your cloud array with whom you share a language.

Toxic Mist Requires malignant mist): The nanocyte’s malignant mist deals half damage on a successful Fortitude save. Creatures who fail their Fortitude save against malignant mist become sickened for a number of rounds equal to the nanocyte’s level.
Sheath Array Improvements
Agile Host: The nanocyte adds her insight bonus from her sheath array to initiative checks.

Extensive Reach: When the nanocyte’s sheath array is active, her reach increases by 5 feet.
Facial Reconfiguration Requires versatile nanites (Disguise): While the nanocyte’s sheath array is active, she can use the Disguise skill to change her appearance with 1 minute of work; she can spend a spell point to reduce this required time to a full-round action. She reduces the Disguise check’s total DC modifiers by an amount equal to 1/2 her nanocyte level (to a minimum of +0).
Grant Sheath: The nanocyte may form her sheath array on a touched ally rather than herself, granting them its benefits for as long as the sheath remains active and the ally remains within 10 feet of the nanocyte. Effects which extend the range of the nanocyte’s nanite array extend the range of this ability by an equal amount.

Swarm Strike: While the nanocyte’s sheath array is active, she may use her casting ability modifier in place of her Strength or Dexterity modifier when making attack and damage rolls with unarmed strikes. This improvement may be taken a second time, in which case the nanocyte’s unarmed strike gains the reach special feature and can be thrown for as long as her sheath array is active. The range increment of these thrown unarmed strikes is 20 feet per 6 nanocyte levels.
Versatile Nanites: The nanocyte adds her insight bonus from her sheath array to two of the following skills: Bluff, Craft (any), Disable Device, Disguise, Heal, Perception, or Piloting. This improvement may be selected multiple times, each time selecting two different skills.
Quick Nanites (Ex)

At 15th level, the nanocyte may summon or switch equipment onto herself, alter a nanite array, or dismiss a nanite array as an immediate action or free action.

This alters quick summons.

Immortality Protocol (Ex)

At 20th level, when the nanocyte would die, she may spend 3 spell points to activate an immortality protocol even when she could not take actions. At the beginning of her next turn, the nanocyte’s body and equipment disperse into a nanite mist and reform her upright in a position of her choice within close range. The nanocyte reappears upright while wielding any combination of equipment in her possession, and she is set to half her maximum hit points. The nanocyte can then act on her turn as normal.

As an immediate action, the nanocyte may use this ability on an adjacent ally when they die. If she spends additional spell points with this ability, she can instead target an ally up to 20 feet away for each additional spell point spent.

This replaces infinite arsenal.

Nanocyte Arsenal Tricks

The following arsenal tricks are exclusive to the nanocyte.

Buoying Nanites (requires Telekinesis sphere): When the nanocyte attempts to lift one or more targets which are in the area of her nanite cloud, she treats her nanocyte level as her caster level for the purpose of determining the size of the target she can lift.
Clinging Nanites (Ex) Whenever the nanocyte damages a target with her hungry shroud, malignant mist, one of her bound weapons, or a natural attack or touch attack while wearing her nanite sheath, she may spend a spell point to attach nanites to them. These nanites resonate with the rest of her nanite array, allowing her to sense the target as though she had blindsight out to medium range. In addition, she can track the target with a base DC of 10 regardless of the surface conditions, and she can use Perception in place of Survival to track the target. The tracking nanites remain active for a number of days equal to her casting ability modifier.
Complex Formation (Ex) (Requires armorist 6): The nanocyte may have both of her nanite arrays active at once. If she possesses the limited nanites limitation, she may have one of her nanite arrays active at the same time as one instance of her summon equipment ability.
Defensive Dispersal (Ex) By spending a spell point as an immediate action when she takes damage, the nanocyte may reduce the damage dealt to her by an amount equal to her nanocyte level + her casting ability modifier. If the triggering effect also requires a saving throw, the nanocyte gains a +1 circumstance bonus on the first saving throw against the effect (such as the initial saving throw to resist a poison, but not subsequent saves against it). The nanocyte may take this arsenal trick a second time starting at 10th level, in which case the damage is reduced by twice her nanocyte level + her casting ability modifier.
Fluid Form (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal, reactive spray): When the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal, she may use reactive spray as part of the same immediate action.
Fuel for the Fires (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal): When the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal to reduce the damage, she enhances the next attack she makes with a summoned equipment before the end of her next turn. If the attack hits, it deals 1d6 additional damage (or 1d4 additional damage if the weapon attacks all creatures in an area). This additional damage increases by 1d6 (or 1d4 for attacks against an area) at 9th level, 13th level, and 17th level. Alternatively, when a creature takes damage from the nanocyte’s malignant mist or hungry shroud the nanocyte can expend her absorbed energy to increase the damage the creature takes by 1d6 (increased to 2d6 at 9th level, 3d6 at 13th level, and 4d6 at 17th level). Either form of additional damage is of the same type as the attack’s normal damage.
Group Dispersal (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal): The nanocyte can use her defensive dispersal on any ally she can see who’s adjacent to her or within her cloud array. When a nanocyte uses defensive dispersal on herself, any adjacent allies also gain the benefits of that ability against the triggering attack or effect. For every additional spell point spent when using defensive dispersal, one protected ally benefits from any additional arsenal tricks when the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal.
Healing Nanites (Su) When the nanocyte spends a spell point on an ability which uses her cloud array, sheath array, or defensive dispersal arsenal trick, she restores hit points equal to 1/2 her nanocyte level.
Kinetic Surge (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal): When the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal to prevent damage, she gains a +10 foot bonus to her movement speeds and a +2 bonus to AC against attacks of opportunity until the end of her next turn. These bonuses increase to 20 feet and +4 if the nanocyte still took damage greater than her level.
Nanite Merger (Ex) The nanocyte gains the Alteration sphere as a bonus talent, taking the Lycanthropic drawback and Swarm Shape as her bonus talent. When she assumes the Gaseous Body form, she may occupy space as per her nanite cloud and may apply any cloud array improvements to herself. If she possesses the grant sheath improvement and has the Gaseous Body trait, she may merge herself with the sheath array for as long as her shapeshift lasts, sharing a space with her ally and gaining improved cover for as long as the granted sheath array remains on them.
Rebounding Strike (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal): When the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal, she may spend an additional spell point to send the damage back at the attacker. If the attacker is within close range, they take damage equal to the damage negated by defensive dispersal (Fortitude save negates). The save DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 the nanocyte’s level + her casting ability modifier.
Triune Formation (Ex) (requires armorist 12, complex formation, limited nanites): The nanocyte may have both of her nanite arrays active at the same time as one instance of her summon equipment ability.
Turnabout (Ex) (requires defensive dispersal and rebounding strike): The nanocyte’s saving throw bonus from defensive dispersal increases by 2. If the nanocyte negates damage using defensive dispersal or succeeds at a saving throw against a non-damaging effect which she used defensive dispersal on, she may use rebounding strike to deal 1d6 points of damage per 2 nanocyte levels to a single target within close range. The target is allowed a Fortitude save as normal.
Vast Improvements: The nanocyte selects an additional sheath array or cloud array improvement. This arsenal trick can be selected multiple times.
Warding Dispersal (Su) (requires defensive dispersal, Protection sphere): When the nanocyte uses defensive dispersal, she may spend an additional spell point to target herself with an aegis as part of the same action. This aegis costs spell points as normal.
Arsenal Tricks

The following arsenal tricks are available to all armorists.

Advanced Armaments: The armorist can call more advanced armor and weaponry. When using summon equipment to call weapons which would have an enhancement bonus, the armorist may reduce the enhancement bonus of the summoned weapon in order to call a weapon worth a number of enhancement bonus points equal to the value of enhancement bonus sacrificed from the soulknife’s Emulate Technological Melee Weapon* or Emulate Technological Ranged Weapon* blade skills table. The armorist cannot reduce a weapon’s enhancement bonus below +1.
Agile Armor: The armorist’s bound and summoned gear gains the floating and landing special abilities. The armorist adds quickness (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor.
Burdensome Attacks: The armorist adds gravitation* (+3), mire* (+1), and wrenching (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Consumptive Armaments: The armorist adds bodyfeeder (+3), mindfeeder (+3), mindspiking* (+3), and soulbreaker (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons. If she is wielding this equipment, she may use her own Death sphere save DC in place of the save DC listed in these special abilities.
Disruptive Defenses: The armorist adds gleaming (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and greater murmuring (+2) and murmuring (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and shields.
Easy Armor: The armorist adds spellroom* (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and fusing (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and shields.
Energized Armaments: The armorist adds energized* and hybridized* to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons, using the weapons’ normal bonus costs for whatever weapon and energy type are used.
Executioner: The armorist adds coup de grace (+5), disruption (+2), and heart-piercing (+5) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons. If she is wielding this equipment, she may use her own Death sphere save DC in place of the save DC listed in these special abilities.
Fully Loaded: The armorist adds automatic* (+1), expanded capacity* (+1), and greater expanded capacity* (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Grenadier (requires armorist 6): The armorist may use summon equipment to summon an arc grenade, bang grenade, concussion grenade, EMP grenade, flash grenade, flechette grenade, fragmentation grenade, inferno grenade, soft grenade, or zero grenade in place of a weapon, shield, or suit of armor. These grenades gain enhancement bonuses as normal for summoned weapons, and the armorist may select grenades as bound equipment. Any grenades created through summon equipment have a saving throw DC of 10 + 1/2 the armorist’s level + her casting ability modifier in place of their normal DC.
Grenadier, Experimental (requires armorist 10, grenadier): The armorist may use summon equipment ability to summon an atom grenade, bio grenade, plasma grenade, gravity grenade, or sonic grenade .
Heavy Impact: The armorist adds collision (+2), psychokinetic (+1), and psychokinetic burst (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Heavy Ordnance: The armorist adds array* (+1), burst* (+1), exploding* (+2), greater array* (+3), and greater exploding* (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons. If she is wielding this equipment, she may use her own Destruction sphere save DC in place of the save DC listed in these special abilities.
Modification Expert: The armorist may add any number of weapon modifications to her bound or summoned weapons at a total cost of a +1 bonus to the weapon. She may increase the cost to +2 to retain proficiency with the weapon regardless of how many modifications are added.
Overclocked Armaments Requires advanced armaments, armorist 10: When using advanced armaments to call non-bound technological weapons, the armorist may spend an additional spell point to increase the summoned weapon’s final enhancement bonus by 1, to a limit of the weapon’s normal maximum enhancement bonus. For example, a 12th-level armorist could use this ability to summon a +1 rail gun (which would normally be a +0 rail gun and could not be summoned), but not a +4 flare gun (since she cannot summon a +4 weapon at 12th level).
Overload Specialist: The armorist adds boosting* (+1), conduit* (+3), kicking* (+2), and wideshot* (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Piercing Specialist: The armorist adds armor penetration* (+1), and puncturing* (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Psibreaker: The armorist adds mindcrusher (+2), psibane (+2), and psychodisruptive (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons. If she is wielding this equipment, she may use her own Mana sphere save DC in place of the save DC listed in these special abilities.
Ramping Assault: The armorist adds furyborn (+2), linked striking (+2), and polarizing* (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Shattering Armaments: The armorist adds dissipater (+1), sundering (+1), and vibrating* (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Spelltank: The armorist adds radiant (+4) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and blastproof* (+3) and mindarmor (+3) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor and shields.
Tools of the Trade: The armorist’s bound and summoned weapons gain the professional* special ability.
Trick Shooter: The armorist adds flexible* (+4), grazing* (+2), and selective* (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons.
Unseen Killer: The armorist adds injecting* (+1), sniper* (+1), and subtle* (+2) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons. If she is wielding this equipment, she may use her own Illusion sphere save DC in place of the save DC listed in these special abilities.
Vigilant Arsenal: The armorist adds guardian (+1), and parrying (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned weapons and seeing (+1) to the list of special abilities she may add to her bound and summoned armor.
